title: Progressive waves
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; W01-uk1#t3 term and clue written for the game; W01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W01-uk1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W01-1#N.1, W01-uk1#N.3, W01-1#N.15, W01-uk1#N.5, W01-uk1#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Amplitude
items.clue: Maximum displacement of a particle from its rest position.

items.label: In phase
items.clue: Relation between points one wavelength apart, which move exactly together.

items.label: Longitudinal wave
items.clue: Has oscillations parallel to the direction of energy transfer, as in sound.

items.label: Phase difference
items.clue: Angle equal to 2π times separation over λ; 90° for points a quarter of a cycle apart.

questions.stem: A loudspeaker plays a steady note to a listener 5 m away in a room with still air. Which of the following travels from the loudspeaker to the listener?

options.text: Energy, passed along by air molecules that vibrate about fixed positions
Air molecules, pushed across the room from the loudspeaker to the ear
Sound particles, which the loudspeaker gives off and the air carries
An electromagnetic signal, which needs no air to carry it across

questions.stem: Two points on a progressive wave of wavelength 1.2 m are 0.40 m apart along the direction of travel. What is the phase difference between their oscillations?
questions.explanation: Right. Δx/λ = 0.40/1.2 = ⅓ cycle, and ⅓ × 2π = 2π/3 rad (120°).

questions.stem: A vibrator sends waves along a stretched string at constant tension. At 25 Hz the wavelength is 0.80 m. The frequency is raised to 100 Hz. What is the new wavelength, and how long does a wave now take to travel 4.0 m along the string?
questions.explanation: v = fλ = 25 × 0.80 = 20 m s⁻¹, unchanged. New λ = 20/100 = 0.20 m; time = 4.0/20 = 0.20 s, the same as before.

questions.stem: Two displacement–time graphs, P and Q, show the oscillations of two points on a wave. Both have a period of 6.0 ms. Each crest of Q comes 1.0 ms after the matching crest of P. What is the phase difference between P and Q?

A loudspeaker emits a steady 500 Hz note. Two microphones are placed on a straight line from the loudspeaker, 0.17 m apart. The speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹. How do the oscillations detected by the two microphones compare?

options.text: They are in antiphase, π rad apart.
They are a quarter of a cycle, π/2 rad, apart.
They are in phase, as the note has one frequency.
They are an eighth of a cycle, π/4 rad, apart.
